8: Asia made what Europe wanted: spices, textiles, silk, tea. Many middlemen, huge profit; Da Gama's 1498 cargo sold at 800% profit. Then in 1453 the road was cut.
In 1453 the Ottomans captured Constantinople and blocked the land routes. Necessity drove the Age of Discovery, led by Portugal and Spain, with the compass, astrolabe and caravel.
Two rivals claimed one ocean, so Pope Alexander VI mediated Tordesillas 1494. East of the line went to Portugal, west to Spain; Brazil's tip fell on the Portuguese side.
Da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, with no factory. Cabral built factories in 1500 (Cochin was permanent); 1503 Albuquerque built Fort Manuel at Cochin, the first European fort.
Almeida 05-09 chose sea power (Blue Water Policy) and forced a Cartaz on ships. Albuquerque 09-15 took Goa in 1510; Nuno da Cunha 29-38 made Goa the HQ in 1530.
Force and the Goa Inquisition (1560-1812) bred resistance. Xavier died in 1552. Marathas, religious backlash, corruption, the English and Dutch, and overextension ended Portugal.
After the 1588 Armada, British and Dutch ships sailed east. The VOC (1602) was the first joint-stock company; it lost at Colachel 1741 and Bedara 1759, and was dissolved in 1799.
The EIC began on 31 December 1600 with Elizabeth I 58-03's Charter. James I 03-25 made it perpetual (1609), Cromwell 51-60 joint-stock (1657); Charles II 60-85's 1661 Charter made it a quasi-State.
Hawkins failed at Jahangir 05-27's court (1608). Best won Swally 1612, then a Farman for Surat (1613). Roe (1615-19) won the Farman of 1618 for trade across the empire.
1661 dowry of Catherine of Braganza gave England Bombay; the Crown passed it to the EIC in 1668. Presidencies: Surat 1618, Madras, Bombay 1687, Calcutta 1699/1700, each grew into a province.
Danes (1616, Tranquebar 1620) sold their posts by 1845. French company 1664, Pondicherry 1674, capital under Francois Martin 01-06. Order of arrival is a favourite Prelims test.
9: A profit company, the EIC, ruled 63% of India's land by 1857. The 1661 Charter gave forts, troops, courts; wars were for trade or for territory.
Aurangzeb 58-07 crushed the EIC in Child's War (1686-90) and pardoned it for Rs 1.5 lakh. The 1691 Farman gave duty-free trade in Bengal for Rs 3,000 a year.
Dupleix 42-54 led the French EIC from 1742, dreaming of empire. Three Carnatic Wars: 1746-48, 1749-54, 1756-63. The 1st and 3rd are global spillovers, the 2nd is factionalism.
Dupleix 42-54 took Madras; at Adyar 1746 about 1,000 French-trained troops beat Anwaruddin 44-49's 10,000 cavalry. Indian kings now wanted European help to modernise armies.
Aix-La-Chapelle 1748 ended the war and returned Madras to the EIC. Nothing changed in territory; Dupleix 42-54 was left empty-handed, so he looked for new quarrels.

Two quarrels, four claimants: Md Ali 52-95 against Chanda Sahib 49-52 in Carnatic; Nasir Jung 48-50 against Muzaffar Jung 50-51 in Hyderabad. French back Chanda and Muzaffar; the EIC backs the others.
The French won first: Chanda Sahib 49-52 became Nawab and Muzaffar Jung 50-51 Nizam. Dupleix 42-54's model: succession dispute, army at State cost, land as payment, a Resident.
Dupleix 42-54 left Arcot unguarded; Clive 57-67 took it in 1751 and held it 53 days. Paris refused help; Treaty of Pondicherry 1754 recalled Dupleix 42-54.
The Seven Years' War (1756-63) brought royal armies. Clive 57-67 took the Northern Sarkars in 1759; Eyre Coote won Wandiwash on 22 January 1760; Pondicherry fell 1761.
Paris 1763: France lost its gains since 1749, kept five posts and could not fortify. The EIC won all three wars on money, leadership and navy, and held the trade monopoly.
Royal armies plus Clive 57-67's diplomacy made Plassey 1757 possible. Later SAs followed: Hyderabad 1798, Mysore 1799, Travancore 1805. The French founded the model; the British used it.
10: The EIC was a trader with Farmans. Dr Hamilton cured Farrukhsiyar 13-19, so the 1717 Farman gave duty-free trade, the Royal Mint and 38 villages. The Nawab had to honour it.
MQK 17-27 allowed duty-free trade but no Dastak misuse, refused the Royal Mint, and allowed renting villages, not buying. So EIC officers looked for other ways to profit.
Officers misused the Dastak, the duty-free pass, for private trade: 1,00,000 pounds a year by 1750, about 50 times their salaries. Bengal lost revenue.
Alivardi Khan 40-56 tolerated it. Siraj 56-57 stopped the Dastak misuse, seized Kasimbazar and Calcutta (renamed Alinagar). The Black Hole story was born.
Clive 57-67 came from Madras with the Royal military, retook Calcutta, signed the Treaty of Alinagar, beat the French at Chandarnagar. Now he needed a way to beat Siraj by a deal.
Mir Jafar 57-60, Siraj's Bakshi, made a deal with Clive 57-67. At Plassey, 23 June 1757, most of the army did not fight; Siraj fled and was beheaded by Miran.
The reward: cash to the Royal military, to Clive 57-67 and to the EIC, plus untaxed Gomasta trade. Gold went to Britain (the Drain). Mir Qasim 60-63 replaced Mir Jafar 57-60.
Mir Qasim 60-63 moved to Bihar, punished underreporting zamindars and abolished internal duties. Beaten in 1763, he fled to Awadh and joined Shuja 54-75 and Shah Alam II 60-06.
At Buxar 1764, Hector Munroe won against Shuja 54-75, Shah Alam II 60-06 and Mir Qasim 60-63. Clive 57-67 was in London. It was the EIC's first real military victory.
Allahabad 1765: Paper, the Emperor gets Allahabad and Kora. Power, the EIC gets the Diwani and Dual Government. Pay, Awadh pays Rs 50 lakh and becomes a buffer.
The Great Bengal Famine 1770 killed about one-third of the people and nobody took charge. The EIC went bankrupt in 1772; W. Hastings 73-85 brought Direct Rule.
11: Richard Wellesley 98-05 became Governor General in 1798, an empire builder. Brother Arthur commanded the 33rd Foot (Royal, not EIC); Henry did administration and diplomacy. He founded Fort William College in 1800.
GBF 1770 led to bankruptcy in 1772 and the Regulating Act 1773. Wars (1775-82, 1780-84) cost money, so Pitt's India Act 1784 banned conquest. Richard needed a big threat.
Napoleon attacked Egypt in 1798 and was in contact with Tipu 82-99. Wellesley 98-05 overhyped the threat; Britain's navy was superior. The British State agreed anyway, wanting a cheaper path.
Britain wanted no risks. Wellesley 98-05 offered the Subsidiary Alliance: control without annexation. The idea was older: Dupleix 42-54 at Hyderabad in 1751 and Clive 57-67 at Awadh in 1765.
Wellesley 98-05 wrote it as a model treaty. The EIC gets five things: Resident, military alliance, State army disbanded, subsidy, Foreign Policy. The ruler gets two: protection, non-interference.
Rulers signed for protection against revolts and neighbours, a subsidy cheaper than annexation, royal dignity and help in succession disputes. The teacher tags the fifth as FACTIONALISM.
The chain: the State army is disbanded, the EIC army grows, the subsidy rises, taxes rise, peasants revolt, land is taken for cash, and no alliances remain. Control without annexation bites.
Hyderabad signed first in 1798, Mysore 1799, Awadh 1801, Gaikwad and Peshwa Bajirao II 96-18 in 1802, Scindia 1803, Jats, Rajputs and Bundelas 1803-05, Travancore 1805.
Wellesley 98-05 also annexed: Mysore land 1799, half of Awadh 1801, the Carnatic 1801. In the 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (1803-05) Bhonsle lost Orissa and Scindia lost Delhi.
Wars cost money again: 4th Anglo-Mysore War 1799 and 2nd Anglo-Maratha War 1803-05. Wellesley 98-05 was recalled to London. Travancore 1805 was his last SA.
Under Francis Hastings 13-23 came the last two: Bhonsle 1816 and Holkar 1818. Ten SAs in 20 years: eight under Wellesley 98-05, two under Francis Hastings 13-23.
12: Hyder Ali 61-82 and Tipu 82-99 used Military Fiscalism: maximise revenue for a stronger army. France gave arms for trade; Tipu ran a State trading company. Four neighbours feared Mysore.
Hyder Ali 61-82 annexed Malabar and Calicut in 1766. The EIC and Hyderabad signed the Treaty of Hyderabad, the EIC getting the Northern Sarkars; the Marathas joined, a triple alliance.
Hyder paid the Marathas Rs 35 lakh and the Nizam Rs 20 lakh to break the alliance. In 1769 he reached Madras's gates. Treaty of Madras: territories returned. Mysore won.
In 1771 the Marathas attacked Mysore and the EIC refused help, so the 1769 alliance was empty. In 1779 the EIC seized Mahe, Hyder's French arms route.
Hyder invaded the Carnatic. At Pollilur 1780 his rockets destroyed Baillie's force. Nana Fadnis built a Triple Confederacy of Marathas, Mysore and Hyderabad (1780-82).
Warren Hastings 73-85 returned Guntur to Hyderabad and signed Salbai 1782 with the Marathas. Mysore was alone. Hyder died; Tipu 82-99 ended it at Mangalore 1784, a stalemate.
Tipu 82-99 attacked Travancore, an EIC ally; Cornwallis 86-93 declared war with the Marathas and Hyderabad. Seringapatam 1792: Tipu lost half his Kingdom, paid 3 crore, gave two sons.
Tipu 82-99's talks with Napoleon gave Wellesley 98-05 his pretext. Hyderabad fought under its SA of 1798. Tipu died at Seringapatam; the Wodeyars returned under an SA.
Mysore lost for four reasons: no stable alliance, a French naval gap, Military Fiscalism over-extension, and a Seringapatam three armies could surround. It fought well but largely alone.
Dhondia Wagh, with soldiers disbanded under the SA, raided until Arthur Wellesley killed him in 1800. In 1801 Wellesley 98-05 annexed the Carnatic for debts and secret contact with Tipu 82-99.
Marthanda Varma 29-58 beat the Dutch at Colachel 1741. Rama Varma 58-98's EIC alliance hedged against Mysore; the 1805 SA with Wellesley 98-05 was the price of crushing a Nair revolt.
Velu Thampi Dalawa rose against the subsidy and interference with the Kundara Proclamation (January 1809). It was crushed. With Cochin's SA, the EIC was paramount from the Krishna to Kanyakumari.
